sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 2.8. Let v be any friendly place of K, lying above the prime p of Q. For any continuous character η : Gal(K̄/K) → Q_p^*, ramified at only finitely many places, pure of weight w, and locally algebraic at each prime above p, one has η²|_{K_v^*} = χ · Norm_{K_v/Q_p}^w, where χ has finite order. In particular, w is even and the Hodge–Tate weight of η at the place v equals w/2.
sourceIssues.correction: The identity holds on the local units: η²|_{O_{K_v}^*} = χ · Norm_{K_v/Q_p}^w with χ of finite order. It does not hold on all of K_v^*. The final sentence — w even, Hodge–Tate weight w/2 at v — is correct, and is what Lemmas 2.9 and 2.10 use.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample: K = Q (which has no CM subfield, so every finite place is friendly), v = p, η = χ_cyc^{-1}. Then η is ramified only at p, locally algebraic there, and pure of weight w = 2, since geometric Frobenius at ℓ acts by ℓ. As an idele class character η(p) = 1, because the local Artin image of a uniformizer acts trivially on μ_{p^∞} in either normalisation; so η²(p) = 1 while Norm_{Q_p/Q_p}(p)^w = p², and χ(p) = p^{-2} has infinite order. On units η(u) = u and η² = Norm², so the identity does hold there. The proof cannot give more: local algebraicity is the hypothesis that η_p 'agrees, in a neighbourhood of the identity, with the Q_p-points of an algebraic homomorphism' (p. 12), and the closing step — 'any Q_p-rational character of (Res_{E/Q} G_m)^1 is trivial upon pullback to E_v^*' — is a statement about that algebraic character, hence controls η only on an open subgroup of E_v^*, not on a uniformizer.

sourceIssues.printed: We can choose this basis in such a way that all powers β_1β_2^j with j non-negative are represented by simple closed curves on T°, which start and end at p.
sourceIssues.correction: Give a construction. The curves can be produced as the images of β_1 under powers of the Dehn twist about β_2, which carries simple closed curves to simple closed curves and sends β_1 to a representative of β_1β_2^j.
sourceIssues.reason: The assertion is made without proof or reference, and the accompanying Figure 5 draws only some of the curves. It carries the rest of Lemma 8.11: the curves γ_{j*} are defined as β_1β_2^j for j ∈ [0, q], and Lemma 8.11 is in turn what the proof of Lemma 8.10 — hence of Lemma 8.9, hence of Theorem 8.1 — rests on. The assertion is true: on a once-punctured torus β_1β_2^j is a primitive class, hence represented by a simple closed curve, and the representatives can be taken through the base point p.
